unit.title: Provide temporary epilation and bleaching treatments

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the difference between epilation and depilation?
options: Epilation removes hair from the root; depilation removes it at the surface
Epilation removes hair at the surface; depilation removes it from the root
Epilation is permanent; depilation lasts for about six months
There is no difference: both words mean shaving the skin

questions.stem: Which of these is a temporary epilation method?
options: Shaving with a razor
Using a depilatory cream
Waxing or sugaring
Trimming with scissors

questions.stem: In this unit, what does a 'bleaching' treatment do?
options: It lightens the colour of the client's skin all over
It lightens dark hair so that it shows less
It removes the hair from the root, like wax
It kills germs on the treatment couch

questions.stem: What are the three stages of the hair growth cycle, in order?
options: Telogen, anagen, catagen
Catagen, telogen, anagen
Vellus, terminal, lanugo
Anagen, catagen, telogen

questions.stem: Why does hair not all grow back at the same time after waxing?
options: The wax damages some follicles more than others
Hair only grows back at night, while the client is asleep
The client used the wrong soap after waxing
Each hair is at a different stage of its growth cycle

questions.stem: Which type of hair is fine, soft and short, and covers most of the body?
options: Terminal hair
Vellus hair
Lanugo hair
Pubic hair

questions.stem: Why must you ask a client whether she uses any skin creams or tablets from her doctor before waxing?
options: Some medicines, such as retinoids, thin the skin so it can tear
Medicines make the wax melt at a much lower temperature
The doctor must always be paid before the client is waxed
Some medicines make the hair grow straight back on the same day

questions.stem: A client has varicose veins on her lower legs. What should you do?
options: Wax over them firmly so the veins go down
Use hotter wax on the veins than on the rest of the leg
Do not wax over them; work only on the clear areas
Wax the veins first, before the rest of the leg

questions.stem: Which condition stops a waxing treatment on that area, so the client is referred to a doctor?
options: Dark, coarse hair on both of the lower legs
Hair that is about 1 cm long
A skin infection, such as boils or impetigo
Dry skin that needs a moisturiser

questions.stem: A client with diabetes asks for a leg wax. What is the safest approach?
options: Take extra care and ask for her doctor's approval first
Wax as normal, because diabetes does not affect the skin
Use extra hot wax, because her skin will not feel it
Wax only the areas where she has lost all feeling

questions.stem: Why should a mole or a skin tag be left out when waxing?
options: The wax will make the mole change colour at once
The hair on a mole grows back too quickly
Moles make the wax set too fast to remove
The wax can pull and tear it, causing bleeding

questions.stem: Why is a small test patch of wax done on the client before a full waxing treatment?
options: To find out how much the treatment should cost
To check her skin's reaction to the heat and the wax
To see whether the wax is the right colour for her
To warm up the wax before it is put back into the heater pot

questions.stem: When should a skin test for a hair bleach usually be done?
options: About 24 to 48 hours before, as the maker states
Straight after the bleach is removed
Only if the client asks for one at the front desk
One whole year before her very first treatment

questions.stem: How should you test the temperature of warm wax before it touches the client?
options: Dip your fingertip straight into the pot of wax for a second
Put a little on the client's face, where the skin is thin
Look at it closely; if it runs off the spatula, it is safe
Test it on your inner wrist, then on a small area of her skin

questions.stem: Which practice keeps a wax heater safe to use?
options: Leave it switched on overnight so it is ready in the morning
Keep it on the floor so it cannot be knocked off a trolley
Use it on a stable trolley with its cable tidy
Fill it to the very top so that it heats more quickly

questions.stem: What is the main danger if wax is heated above the maker's working temperature?
options: The wax will lose its colour
It can burn the client's skin
The wax will stop the hair growing
The strips will not stick together

questions.stem: Hot wax burns a client's skin. What is the correct first aid?
options: Rub some butter or cooking oil on the burn straight away
Burst any blisters with a pin and cover them with a plaster
Put ice straight on the skin for an hour
Cool it under cool running water and get first aid help

questions.stem: Why must a spatula never be put back into the wax pot once it has touched the client's skin?
options: It can carry germs from the skin into the wax
It will make the wax too cool to work with
It will make the wax change to a darker colour
It will make the spatula break into pieces

questions.stem: What should happen to strip wax that has been removed from a client?
options: Melt it down and use it again for the next client
Put it with the strip in a lined, lidded bin
Keep it in a jar to show the next client
Wash it off the strip and reuse the strip

questions.stem: Why should the therapist wear disposable gloves during waxing?
options: To keep her hands warm in a cold treatment room all day
To stop the wax from sticking to the spatula
To protect both of them from germs and blood spots
To make the wax strips easier to pull off

questions.stem: Before applying warm wax, why is the skin cleaned with a pre-wax lotion?
options: To remove oil, sweat and creams so that the wax grips the hair
To add a layer of oil to the skin so that the strip slides off well
To make the hairs longer so that they are easier to grip
To numb the skin so that the client feels nothing

questions.stem: A client's leg hair is about 3 cm long. What should you do before waxing?
options: Wax it as it is, using a thicker layer of wax
Ask her to shave first and come back the next day
Pull the long hairs out with tweezers before waxing
Trim it shorter with clean scissors first

questions.stem: In which direction is warm (strip) wax applied?
options: Against the direction of hair growth
In circles, to cover the area evenly
In the same direction as the hair grows
Across the hair, from side to side

questions.stem: How should a wax strip be removed?
options: Slowly, pulling it straight up and away from the skin
Quickly, against the hair growth and close to the skin
Slowly, in the same direction as the hair growth
Quickly, straight up towards the ceiling

questions.stem: Why do you hold the skin taut (stretched firm) while removing a strip?
options: So the wax goes back into the pot more easily
So that the hair grows back thicker and darker the next time
To reduce pain and stop bruising or lifting of the skin
To keep the client from moving her leg off the couch

questions.stem: Straight after removing a strip, why do you press your hand firmly on the area?
options: To soothe the skin and ease the stinging
To push the hairs back into the follicles
To spread the wax that is left on the skin
To check that the skin is still warm

questions.stem: How is hot (hard) wax removed?
options: With a paper strip pressed firmly onto the wax
By flicking up its edge once set, without a strip
By softening it with plenty of warm soapy water on a sponge
By scraping it off with a sharp metal blade

questions.stem: Why is hot (hard) wax often chosen for the underarm and bikini line?
options: It is cheaper and quicker to use than any other kind of wax
It is applied cold, so it cannot burn the skin at all
It removes the hair for ever after only one treatment
It grips short, coarse hair and is gentler on delicate skin

questions.stem: Why should the underarm be waxed in small sections?
options: The hair often grows in more than one direction
The underarm has no hair follicles at all
Sections let the wax cool down more quickly
So that the client is able to lift her arm up higher

questions.stem: Which statement about sugaring paste is correct?
options: It is made from rubber and is used only on the scalp
It is a chemical cream that dissolves the hair at the surface
It is a sugar-based paste that removes hair from the root
It is a powder that bleaches the hair a lighter colour

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should be given for the first 24 to 48 hours after waxing?
options: Go to the beach and lie in the sun so that the redness calms down
Avoid heat, sun, perfumed products and tight clothing
Scrub the area hard each day with a coarse scrub
Shave any hairs that are left the same evening

questions.stem: How can a client help to prevent ingrown hairs between waxing treatments?
options: Shave the area every day between waxes
Pick out any of the hairs that are trapped under the skin with pins
Avoid washing the area for a full week
Exfoliate gently a few days after waxing, then regularly

questions.stem: After waxing, about how long does it usually take for the hair to grow back enough to wax again?
options: Only one or two days
About one whole year
About six months or more
About four to six weeks

questions.stem: Small red bumps appear over the waxed area straight after treatment. What does this usually mean?
options: The client has a serious infection and must go to hospital
The wax was too cold and must be heated more for next time
A normal short-term reaction to the hair being removed
The hair has grown back already and must be waxed again

questions.stem: What usually causes the top layer of skin to lift (come away) during waxing?
options: Waxing the same area too many times, or on thin skin
Using a new, clean spatula for each dip into the wax pot
Testing the wax on your wrist before use
Applying wax in the direction of hair growth

questions.stem: Tiny spots of blood appear in the follicles after waxing strong hair on the legs. What should you do?
options: Wipe them away with your bare fingers and carry on as normal
With gloves on, wipe with antiseptic on clean cotton
Apply more wax over them to stop the bleeding
Leave them and tell the client to wash at home

questions.stem: Some waxes contain rosin (colophony). Why does this matter at the consultation?
options: Rosin makes the wax smell of pine for the client
Rosin turns the wax red when it is too hot
Some people are allergic to rosin and react to it
Rosin stops the wax from gripping the hair

questions.stem: What is mixed together to make most hair bleach for the face and body?
options: Hydrogen peroxide cream and an activator powder
Fresh lime juice and baking soda from the kitchen
Household laundry bleach mixed with tap water
Wax and talcum powder

questions.stem: Which area must never have hair bleach applied to it?
options: The upper lip
Near the eyes
The forearms
The lower legs

questions.stem: How should the skin be prepared before applying hair bleach?
options: Rub in a rich oil so the bleach slides on easily
Exfoliate hard so the bleach soaks in deeper
Wax the area first, then bleach straight away
Clean it so it is free of grease, and dry it well

questions.stem: Why should you check the bleach every few minutes while it is on the skin?
options: To add more water to the bleach so that it does not dry out at all
To stir it with your finger so that it works evenly
To see how light the hair is and spot any skin reaction
To wipe a little off to give to the next client

questions.stem: A client with very dark skin wants the dark hair on her forearms bleached. What should you discuss with her?
options: Bleached hair can look golden and stand out on dark skin
Bleach will make all of her skin many shades lighter for good
Bleach removes the hair from the root for six months
Bleach works only on clients who are under 30

questions.stem: Which is the safest way to work with hair bleach in the treatment room?
options: Mix it in a metal bowl and leave the lid off the jar
Mix it in a closed room with no air flow, to keep it warm
Mix extra bleach and keep it for the next client's visit
Wear gloves, ventilate the room and mix only what you need

questions.stem: What should be written on the record card after a waxing treatment?
options: Only the client's phone number and the date of her visit
The areas waxed, the wax used and any reaction
The names of the other clients waxed that day
How much hair was removed, weighed in grams

questions.stem: What is the main risk with a depilatory (hair-removing) cream, and how is it reduced?
options: It can make the hair grow back thicker, so use it once a year
It can set hard like wax, so remove it with a strip
It can burn or irritate the skin, so do a skin test first
It can bleach the skin white, so use it only at night

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the resting stage of the hair growth cycle?
What name is given to the thick, coarse, darker hair found under the arms and on the legs?
What flat wooden or plastic tool is used to spread warm wax on the skin?
Into what container should a used razor blade or other sharp item be put?
Name the problem, often seen after shaving or waxing, where a hair curls back and grows under the skin.
What type of product is used after waxing to remove small bits of wax left on the skin?
What is the name of the fabric or paper piece pressed onto warm wax and pulled off to remove it?
What is the name of an infection of the hair follicles that shows as red, pus-filled spots after waxing or shaving?
After hair bleach is removed, should the skin be rinsed with hot water or cool water?
What part of a wax heater keeps the wax at a steady temperature?
What do we call the lotion used to clean the skin of oil, sweat and creams just before waxing?
What is the name of the short in-between stage of the hair cycle, when the hair stops growing and comes away from its blood supply?
What main ingredient, found in every kitchen, is sugaring paste mostly made from?
What do we call a chemical cream that dissolves hair at the surface of the skin?
What document holds the client's details, the contraindication check, the treatments given and her signature?

essays.stem: Describe the three stages of the hair growth cycle and explain why the cycle matters when you advise a client about waxing.
essays.modelAnswer: Hair grows from a follicle in the skin, and each hair goes through a cycle. Anagen is the growing stage: the hair is attached to its blood supply at the base of the follicle and is growing actively. Catagen is a short in-between stage: the hair stops growing and comes away from its blood supply. Telogen is the resting stage: the hair is loose in the follicle until it falls out or is pushed out by a new hair. Every hair on the body is at a different stage at any one time. This means that waxing removes the hairs that are there, but other hairs are still on their way up. So, after a first wax, some hairs appear again quite soon. With regular waxing, about every four to six weeks, the hairs come into step more, and the results look smoother for longer. I explain this so the client knows what to expect and does not shave between treatments.
markingPoints: Anagen: active growing stage
Catagen: short in-between stage, hair comes away from its blood supply
Telogen: resting stage, hair falls out or is pushed out
Hairs are at different stages, so regrowth comes at different times
Advises regular treatments (about every four to six weeks) and no shaving between

essays.stem: Describe the consultation you would carry out before a waxing or bleaching treatment. Include the contraindications you would check for.
essays.modelAnswer: I explain the treatment and fill in the record card with the client. I ask about her medical history, allergies (for example to rosin, plasters or bleach), medicines and creams, including retinoid creams or tablets and blood-thinning medicines, and whether she has diabetes or poor circulation. I ask about recent sunburn, recent treatments such as peels, and how she removes hair now. I look at the area. Infections such as boils, impetigo or fungal infections, open cuts, burns, recent scars and inflamed skin stop the treatment on that area, and I refer her to a doctor where needed. Varicose veins, moles, warts and skin tags are avoided. Thin, fragile skin, diabetes and loss of feeling need extra care and often a doctor's approval. For bleach I do a skin test about 24 to 48 hours before. I agree the plan and the price, and the client signs the card.
markingPoints: Asks about medical history, allergies, medicines (retinoids, blood thinners) and diabetes
Asks about sunburn, recent treatments and hair removal at home
Names conditions that stop the treatment (infections, cuts, burns) and refers
Names conditions to avoid or take care with (varicose veins, moles, thin skin, diabetes)
Skin test for bleach; plan agreed and card signed

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare the wax heater, the work area and the client before a warm wax treatment.
essays.modelAnswer: I put the wax heater on a stable trolley near a socket, with the cable tidy so no one can trip or pull it. I check the plug and cable for damage. I switch it on early and set the thermostat as the maker says, and I never leave it on unattended. I cover the couch with fresh couch roll and protect the floor. I lay out disposable spatulas, strips, pre-wax lotion, after-wax oil, soothing lotion, tweezers, scissors, gloves, cotton and a lined, lidded bin. I wash my hands and put on gloves. After the consultation, I help the client onto the couch and protect her clothing with paper or towels. I clean the area with pre-wax lotion and dry it, and apply a light dusting of powder if the wax maker advises it. I trim very long hair. I stir the wax and test it on my inner wrist, then on a small area of her skin, and I ask her how it feels before I go on.
markingPoints: Heater on a stable surface, cable tidy and checked, thermostat set, never left unattended
Couch and floor protected; tools, products and bin laid out
Hand washing and gloves
Client protected; skin cleaned with pre-wax lotion; long hair trimmed
Wax tested on the therapist's inner wrist, then on a small area of the client's skin

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would carry out a half-leg wax with warm (strip) wax.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation and preparation, the client lies on the couch and I check the direction of hair growth on her lower legs. I test the wax on my inner wrist and then on a small area of her leg. With a new spatula held at an angle, I spread a thin, even layer of wax in the direction of hair growth, over an area a little smaller than the strip. I place the strip on the wax and press it firmly in the direction of growth, leaving a free edge to hold. I hold the skin taut with my other hand and pull the strip off quickly against the direction of growth, keeping it close and parallel to the skin. I press my hand on the area at once to soothe it. I work in an order, front then back, using a new spatula for each dip. I remove any stray hairs with tweezers rather than waxing the same area again and again. I remove wax residue with after-wax oil and finish with a soothing lotion.
markingPoints: Checks hair growth direction and tests the wax temperature
Thin layer applied with a new spatula in the direction of hair growth
Strip pressed on in the direction of growth, with a free edge
Skin held taut; strip removed quickly against growth, close to the skin; pressure applied
No double-dipping, no repeated waxing of one area; residue removed and lotion applied

essays.stem: Compare warm (strip) wax and hot (hard) wax. Say where each is best used, and describe how you would use hot wax on the underarm.
essays.modelAnswer: Warm wax is a soft wax spread thinly and removed with a paper or fabric strip. It is quick for large areas such as the legs and forearms. Hot wax is a thicker wax that sets on the skin and is removed without a strip. It grips short, coarse hair and shrinks around the hair rather than sticking strongly to the skin, so it is gentler on delicate areas such as the underarm, bikini line, upper lip and brows. For the underarm, I ask the client to rest her hand behind her head, clean the area and dry it well. I look at the hair growth, which often grows in two or more directions, and plan small sections. I test the wax on my inner wrist and then on a small area of her skin. I apply a layer of wax in the direction of growth, with a thicker edge to grip. When it has set but is still bendy, I hold the skin taut, flick up the edge and remove it quickly against the growth, close to the skin. I press the area to soothe it.
markingPoints: Warm wax: thin layer, removed with a strip, suits large areas
Hot wax: sets and is removed without a strip, suits short hair and delicate areas
Underarm positioned, cleaned and dried; hair direction checked and worked in sections
Temperature tested; wax applied with growth, with a thick edge
Removed when set but bendy, against growth, skin taut; pressure applied

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep a waxing treatment hygienic, from set-up to clean-up.
essays.modelAnswer: I wash my hands before and after the treatment and wear disposable gloves, because waxing can cause small spots of blood and tissue fluid. I use fresh couch roll and towels for every client. I clean the client's skin with pre-wax lotion. I use a new spatula for every dip into the wax and never put a used spatula back in the pot, so germs from the skin cannot get into the wax. Strips, spatulas, cotton and gloves are used once and put in a lined, lidded bin. Waste with blood on it is sealed in a bag and disposed of as the Centre's rules say. Wax that has touched a client is never reused. Tweezers and scissors are cleaned, then disinfected or sterilised. Any blade goes in the sharps box. At the end I wipe the heater, trolley and couch with a suitable disinfectant, clean wax spills as the maker says, and wash my hands.
markingPoints: Hand washing and disposable gloves, and why
Fresh couch roll and towels; skin cleaned before waxing
New spatula for every dip; no double-dipping; used wax never reused
Single-use items and contaminated waste disposed of correctly; sharps in the sharps box
Tools disinfected or sterilised; heater, trolley and couch cleaned

essays.stem: Describe the contra-actions that can happen during or after waxing, and say what you would do for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Redness and small raised bumps are a normal reaction and usually settle within a few hours; I apply soothing lotion and a cool compress. Blood spots can appear in the follicles where strong hair was removed; with gloves on, I wipe them with antiseptic on clean cotton and dispose of the cotton in a lined, sealed bag. A burn from wax that is too hot must be cooled at once under cool running water, and first aid help sought; I do not put creams or butter on it. Skin can lift or tear if it is thin or waxed too often; I stop, apply a soothing antiseptic and advise her to keep it clean. Bruising comes from not holding the skin taut. An allergic reaction, such as a rash, itching or swelling, means I stop, remove the product and advise her to see a doctor. Ingrown hairs and folliculitis can appear later. I record every contra-action on the record card.
markingPoints: Normal redness and bumps: soothe with lotion or a cool compress
Blood spots: gloves, antiseptic, safe disposal
Burn: cool running water, first aid, no creams or butter
Skin lifting, bruising or allergy: stop, soothe, refer if needed
Records every contra-action

essays.stem: Explain the aftercare and home-care advice you would give after a waxing treatment, and why each point matters.
essays.modelAnswer: For about 24 to 48 hours the follicles are open and the skin is sensitive, so germs can get in and the skin can react. The client should avoid hot baths, saunas, sunbathing, sunbeds and sea or pool swimming, because heat, sun, salt and chlorine can irritate the skin. She should avoid perfumed lotions, and after an underarm wax she should leave out deodorant for a day. She should wear loose, clean clothing to avoid rubbing. She should not touch or scratch the area. After a few days she can exfoliate gently, then do it regularly and moisturise, which helps to stop ingrown hairs. She should not shave between waxes, because shaving cuts the hair and spoils the next wax. Hair usually grows back enough to wax again in about four to six weeks, so I suggest she rebooks then. I tell her to call the salon if she has any lasting redness, spots or soreness, and I record the advice.
markingPoints: Avoid heat, sun, sea and pool for about 24 to 48 hours, and why
Avoid perfumed products and deodorant; loose clothing; no touching
Gentle exfoliation after a few days to prevent ingrown hairs
No shaving between waxes; rebook in about four to six weeks
Report any lasting reaction; advice recorded

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would carry out a hair bleaching treatment on a client's forearms.
essays.modelAnswer: At the consultation I check for contraindications, explain that bleach lightens the hair but does not remove it, and do a skin test about 24 to 48 hours before, as the maker states. On the day I check that the test was negative. I protect the client's clothing and put on gloves. I clean the forearms so they are free of grease and dry them well. In a well-ventilated room, I mix the bleach cream and activator in a non-metallic bowl exactly as the maker says, and mix only what I need. I apply an even layer with a spatula over the hair, keeping it away from any broken skin. I time it as the maker says, and check every few minutes for how light the hair is and for any redness, stinging or itching. If the skin reacts, I remove the bleach at once. When the hair is light enough, I remove the bleach with damp cotton and rinse with cool water. I apply a soothing lotion and record the treatment.
markingPoints: Checks contraindications and a negative skin test done 24 to 48 hours before
Gloves; skin cleaned free of grease and dried
Mixes as the maker says in a non-metallic bowl, in a ventilated room
Applies evenly, times correctly and checks often for colour and reaction
Removes with damp cotton and cool water, applies soothing lotion, records

essays.stem: Explain how hair bleach should be handled, stored and disposed of safely, and what first aid you would give if it reached the client's eyes or caused a skin reaction.
essays.modelAnswer: Hair bleach contains hydrogen peroxide and an activator, so I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. I use only bleach made for face and body hair, never household bleach and never products for lightening the skin. I do not mix brands. I wear gloves and work in a well-ventilated room, because the fumes can irritate the eyes and nose. I mix only what is needed, in a non-metallic bowl, and throw away any leftover, because it cannot be kept. Bleach is stored in its labelled container, with the lid tight, in a cool, dry, dark place away from heat and out of reach of children. Empty containers and used cotton go in a lined, lidded bin. If bleach gets into an eye, I rinse it at once with plenty of clean cool water or eye wash and get medical help. If the skin burns, stings or reddens, I remove the bleach, rinse with plenty of cool water, apply a soothing lotion, record it and advise her to see a doctor if it does not settle.
markingPoints: Uses only products made for hair bleaching; never household bleach; no mixing brands
Gloves and good ventilation
Mixes only what is needed and throws away leftover
Stored in labelled containers, cool, dry and dark; waste disposed of correctly
First aid: rinse eyes or skin with plenty of cool water, get help, record

practical1.title: Half-leg wax with warm (strip) wax
practical1.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client. In a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed to take part. Each member holds a consultation, checks for contraindications and completes the record card. She prepares the wax heater, couch and trolley safely, tests the wax on her own inner wrist and then on a small area of her client's skin, and waxes the client's lower legs (half leg) with warm wax and strips. She removes residue, applies a soothing lotion and gives aftercare advice. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up and checking the heater with the assessor, laying out the trolley, taking the photos, or the final clean-up and waste disposal. Photograph each stage below. Photos show the legs and the work area only. Hand in once for the whole group, with the record cards.
materials: Warm (strip) wax and a wax heater with a thermostat
Pre-wax lotion, after-wax oil and soothing lotion
Tweezers and small scissors (cleaned and disinfected)
Couch with fresh couch roll, towels and protective paper
Salon disinfectant, a lined, lidded bin and the sharps box
photos: The heater on a stable trolley with a tidy cable, and the trolley laid out
The wax being tested on the therapist's inner wrist
One lower leg before waxing, showing the hair growth
Wax applied and the strip in place: close-up
The same area after the strip is removed
The finished leg with soothing lotion applied
The area cleaned, with the waste in a lined, lidded bin
checklist: Held a consultation, checked for contraindications and had the record card signed
Set up the heater safely and tested the wax on the inner wrist, then on the client
Wore gloves and cleaned the skin with pre-wax lotion
Applied a thin, even layer in the direction of hair growth with a new spatula each time
Removed strips quickly against the growth, close to the skin, holding the skin taut
Did not double-dip and did not wax one area again and again
Removed residue, applied soothing lotion and gave aftercare advice
Switched off the heater, disposed of waste correctly and cleaned the area
safety: Test the wax on your inner wrist, then on a small area of the client's skin, before every treatment
Never leave the heater switched on and unattended; keep the cable tidy
If wax burns the skin, cool it at once under cool running water and tell the assessor
Do not wax over varicose veins, moles, cuts or broken skin
Follow the wax maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Hot (hard) wax treatment and a forearm hair bleach
practical2.brief: This task has two parts. Part A: at least 24 to 48 hours before the practical (or as the maker states), each member carries out a skin test for the hair bleach on her client and records it. On the day, if the test is negative, she bleaches the hair on one of her client's forearms following the maker's instructions, checking it often, then removes it and soothes the skin. Part B: each member waxes a small area of her client with hot (hard) wax, either the underarm or the other forearm, as the client prefers. Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client; in a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed. Anyone with a positive skin test is not bleached and does Part B only. Each member also takes one job for the group: mixing and timing the bleach with the assessor watching, checking the hot wax heater, taking the photos, or cleaning up. Photograph each stage below, showing the work area only. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Face and body hair bleach cream and activator, with a non-metallic bowl and spatulas
Hot (hard) wax and a heater with a thermostat
Disposable spatulas, pre-wax lotion, pre-wax oil (if the maker advises), after-wax oil and soothing lotion
Cotton pads, a bowl of cool water and a timer
Disposable gloves and protective paper or towels
Record cards with the skin test results
Salon disinfectant and a lined, lidded bin
photos: Each member's record card showing the bleach skin test date and result (cover private details)
Bleach applied evenly over the hair
Forearm after the bleach is removed, showing the lighter hair
Hot wax applied with a thick edge, in sections
The area after the hot wax is removed
The heater switched off and the area cleaned
checklist: Carried out and recorded a skin test for the bleach at the right time
Mixed the bleach as the maker says, wearing gloves, in a ventilated room
Applied bleach evenly, timed it correctly and checked the skin often
Removed the bleach fully with cool water and applied a soothing lotion
Tested the hot wax on the inner wrist, then on the client, before use
Applied hot wax in the direction of growth and removed it against the growth, skin taut
Gave aftercare advice for both treatments and recorded them
safety: Do not bleach anyone with a positive skin test, broken skin or sunburn
Never use bleach near the eyes; if any gets in an eye, rinse at once with plenty of cool water
Keep the room ventilated and wear gloves when mixing and applying bleach
Test hot wax on your inner wrist, then on the client, and never leave the heater unattended
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for every product
